views.body_sql:

  ball_control,

  agility,

  jumping,

  long_shots,

  FROM Player_Attributes pa
) sub
WHERE row_number = 1

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_identity on player_latest_attributes.player_api_id = player_identity.player_api_id — safe because player_latest_attributes has exactly one row per player_api_id, so attributes are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_latest_attributes only after joining player -> team at a one-to-one level (e.g., if you have a single team_id per player for a snapshot). Joining player_latest_attributes directly to team_latest_attributes on team-level keys is safe only if the join path is one-to-one; otherwise aggregate after the join. | do NOT directly join player_latest_attributes to a one-to-many table/view such as match_lineup_players_unpivot or match_basic_outcomes without re-aggregation or restricting the many-side: those views contain multiple rows per player (matches, lineups, outcomes) and would multiply this view's one-row-per-player measures. If you need player-level aggregates of match data, first aggregate the many-side to one row per player (e.g., COUNT(matches) or AVG(metric) grouped by player_api_id) and then join. | If composing team- or match-level metrics from this view, ensure you aggregate player_latest_attributes after joining if the target grain is team or match (e.g., AVG(overall_rating) GROUP BY team_id). Do not assume team-level uniqueness unless you join via a one-to-one relationship (explicit team assignment table/view). | When joining to sibling aggregated views (e.g., match_team_odds or team_latest_attributes), verify their grains. Joining two one-row-per-entity views on that entity's key (e.g., player_api_id to player_api_id) is safe; joining one-row-per-player (this view) to one-row-per-team (team view) is many-to-one (safe for preserving player rows) but will duplicate team measures per player if you expect a single team row — if you want team measures only once, aggregate players or select distinct team rows instead.

views.description: For each player (player_api_id), pick the most recent Player_Attributes snapshot by date and expose key ratings. Useful when you need a single canonical rating row per player for joins or aggregations (e.g., top players by overall_rating, join player attributes to matches or teams). | Use for: Find top-N players by overall_rating; Join latest player ratings to matches' lineups; Compute average attribute by team using latest player snapshots

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team identity/dimension views on team_api_id — e.g., join to player_identity or any team dimension keyed by team_api_id — safe because team_latest_attributes is one-row-per-team_api_id (its rows will not be duplicated): JOIN team_latest_attributes tla ON tla.team_api_id = dim.team_api_id | safe to join to match-level tables only when the join key is one-to-one per match-team, using match-team keys (match_id + team_api_id) and ensuring match-level rows are unique per team; if match table is one-row-per-team per match, joining on (match_id, team_api_id) is safe because team_latest_attributes remains one row per team and will not multiply measures | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables (e.g., match events, lineups unpivoted, or player tables) on team_api_id without aggregation or deduplication, because those one-to-many relationships will multiply team_latest_attributes rows/measures. Instead: | - When joining to match_lineup_players_unpivot (one-to-many: many players per team per match), aggregate the players side first (e.g., COUNT, AVG) to one row per match+team, then join on (match_id, team_api_id). | - When combining with player_latest_attributes or player_identity, perform the join on player keys when you need player-level rows (accepts multiplication), or pre-aggregate player measures to team level before joining if you want to preserve team-level cardinality. | When composing metrics across time (e.g., attributes as of a match date), this view always returns the latest recorded attribute overall; it is NOT time-travel aware. To avoid temporal mismatch, either filter Team_Attributes by date before taking latest (create a time-bounded view) or join on date-aware keys (e.g., use Team_Attributes directly with date constraints) — otherwise you may incorrectly attribute post-match recorded attributes to earlier matches. | Because the view selects the single ROW_NUMBER()=1 record per team_api_id, joins on team_api_id to dimension tables keyed by team_api_id are safe and will not duplicate measures; any join to tables with multiple rows per team_api_id must be preceded by aggregation/deduplication on that side.

views.description: For each team (team_api_id), return the most recent Team_Attributes snapshot by date including numeric and class fields. Use when you need a single current team profile per team for analysis or joins (e.g., compare team tactics vs match outcomes). | Use for: Join team tactical profiles to matches; Compare teams by buildUpPlaySpeed or chanceCreation metrics; Aggregate team attributes across a league

params.description: An unpivoted roster of match lineups: one row per match, team side, lineup slot and player (home and away), suitable for joining players/teams to match-level data or aggregating per player-slot across matches.
params.when_to_use: Find which player occupied a specific lineup slot for a match (e.g., who was home player in slot 7 for match id X). | Aggregate player participation counts across matches (e.g., how many matches did player P start in any slot, or in a specific slot). | Join per-player attributes (from player_identity or player_latest_attributes) to match-level lineup information. | Join team attributes (from team_latest_attributes) to the team in a match-side lineup row. | Compose match-level outcomes or odds (from match_basic_outcomes or match_team_odds) with the per-player lineup to analyze outcomes by lineup membership.
params.output_schema: id: match row identifier from Match.id. This is the base match table primary key that identifies the match containing the lineup. | match_api_id: match API id from Match.match_api_id (same as id in many contexts), provided to preserve original match identifier present in Match. | side: string literal 'home' or 'away' indicating the team side for this lineup row. In this view only 'home' rows are present (see grounded_columns). | team_api_id: team identifier for the side in the match derived from Match.home_team_api_id (the team that owns the listed home_player_X slots). | player_api_id: player identifier occupying the lineup slot, derived from the corresponding Match.home_player_N column (home_player_1 ... home_player_11). | lineup_slot: integer lineup slot number (1..11) derived from the literal values in each UNION branch representing which home_player_N column supplied player_api_id.
params.grounded_columns: Match.id | Match.match_api_id | Match.home_team_api_id | Match.home_player_1 | Match.home_player_2 | Match.home_player_3 | Match.home_player_4 | Match.home_player_5 | Match.home_player_6 | Match.home_player_7 | Match.home_player_8 | Match.home_player_9 | Match.home_player_10 | Match.home_player_11
params.metric: This view does not define aggregated numeric metrics. It provides descriptive columns at the grain (id, player_api_id, lineup_slot). | Derived boolean/non-NULL filter semantics: row exists iff the corresponding Match.home_player_N IS NOT NULL (i.e., participation in that slot).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_identity on player_api_id — safe because player_identity is (or should be) one-row-per-player_api_id (a dimension). Joining on match_lineup_players_unpivot.player_api_id = player_identity.player_api_id will not duplicate lineup rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_latest_attributes on player_api_id — safe when player_latest_attributes is implemented as one-row-per-player (RANK semantic). This preserves one row per lineup entry. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_latest_attributes on team_api_id — safe because team_latest_attributes is a team-dimension (one-row-per-team_api_id). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_basic_outcomes on Match.id or match_api_id — safe because match_basic_outcomes is normalized to one-row-per-match (NORM). This attaches match-level measures to each lineup row; note that match-level metrics will be duplicated across all lineup rows for that match by design (one lineup row per player), which is correct if you intend per-player participation with match context. | unsafe / cautionary guidance: do NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many fact that contains multiple rows per (match,id) or per (player_api_id,match) without first aggregating the many-side, because such joins will multiply the number of lineup rows and therefore multiply any measures derived from this view. Examples: |  - Do NOT directly join to match_team_odds if match_team_odds contains multiple odds rows per match/team (AGG vs raw) unless you aggregate odds to one row per match+team first. Otherwise odds rows will duplicate lineup rows for that team within the same match. |  - Do NOT directly join to any event/possession or substitution table that has multiple rows per match+player without aggregating/subselecting, because it will multiply counts when computing measures like participation counts. | composition patterns to preserve correctness: |  - To compute per-player counts of matches started: SELECT player_api_id, COUNT(*) FROM match_lineup_players_unpivot GROUP BY player_api_id; |  - To compute per-player match outcomes (win/loss) safely: join match_basic_outcomes (one-row-per-match) on id, then aggregate by player_api_id. This is safe because match_basic_outcomes is one-row-per-match; duplication only arises from the intended lineup multiplicity (one row per player in a match). |  - To combine with a many-row table (e.g., events) aggregate the many-side to the same grain (id, player_api_id) before joining, or aggregate the joined result afterwards using GROUP BY (id, player_api_id) to avoid measure inflation.

views.description: Unpivot Match lineup columns (home_player_1..11 and away_player_1..11) into one row per match-player appearance. Exposes match id, match_api_id, team side (home/away), team_api_id, player_api_id and lineup_slot. Useful when counting appearances, joining player info to appearances, or analyzing player presence per match. | Use for: Count appearances by player or team; Join player attributes to each appearance; Filter matches where a specific player appeared

views.name: match_basic_outcomes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  match_api_id,
  country_id,
  league_id,
  season,
  stage,
  date,
  home_team_api_id,
  away_team_api_id,
  home_team_goal,
  away_team_goal,
  (home_team_goal - away_team_goal) AS goal_difference,
  CASE
    WHEN home_team_goal > away_team_goal THEN 'home_win'
    WHEN home_team_goal = away_team_goal THEN 'draw'
    WHEN home_team_goal < away_team_goal THEN 'away_win'
  END AS match_result,
  B365H,
  B365D,
  B365A
FROM Match

params.description: Provides one-row-per-match basic outcomes and closing odds (score, result, goal difference, and Bet365 closing odds) for matches in the Match table.
params.when_to_use: Get match-level outcome (winner/draw), scoreline, and goal difference for reporting or labeling tasks (e.g., training match outcome models). | Combine match outcomes with team or player attributes to analyze how attributes relate to match results (must respect cardinality guidance). | Join match-level betting odds (B365H/B365D/B365A) with outcomes for betting-performance or calibration analyses. | Filter or aggregate match outcomes by country, league, season, date, stage, or teams (home/away).
params.output_schema: id: Primary key of the match row (Match.id). Unique identifier for this match. | match_api_id: External API identifier for the match (Match.match_api_id). | country_id: Identifier for the country where the match took place (Match.country_id). | league_id: Identifier for the league this match belongs to (Match.league_id). | season: Season label for the match (Match.season). | stage: Stage/round of the competition for the match (Match.stage). | date: Match date (Match.date). | home_team_api_id: API identifier for the home team (Match.home_team_api_id). | away_team_api_id: API identifier for the away team (Match.away_team_api_id). | home_team_goal: Home team's goals scored in the match (Match.home_team_goal). | away_team_goal: Away team's goals scored in the match (Match.away_team_goal). | goal_difference: home_team_goal - away_team_goal (computed from Match.home_team_goal and Match.away_team_goal). Positive => home scored more. | match_result: Categorical result computed as: 'home_win' if home_team_goal > away_team_goal, 'draw' if equal, 'away_win' if home_team_goal < away_team_goal (derived from Match.home_team_goal and Match.away_team_goal). | B365H: Closing home-win decimal odds from Bet365 (Match.B365H). | B365D: Closing draw decimal odds from Bet365 (Match.B365D). | B365A: Closing away-win decimal odds from Bet365 (Match.B365A).
params.grounded_columns: Match.id | Match.match_api_id | Match.country_id | Match.league_id | Match.season | Match.stage | Match.date | Match.home_team_api_id | Match.away_team_api_id | Match.home_team_goal | Match.away_team_goal | Match.B365H | Match.B365D | Match.B365A
params.metric: goal_difference = (Match.home_team_goal - Match.away_team_goal) | match_result = CASE WHEN Match.home_team_goal > Match.away_team_goal THEN 'home_win' WHEN Match.home_team_goal = Match.away_team_goal THEN 'draw' WHEN Match.home_team_goal < Match.away_team_goal THEN 'away_win' END | Note: B365H, B365D, B365A are passed through raw from Match (no aggregation).

SELECT
  id,
  match_api_id,
  home_team_api_id,
  away_team_api_id,
  B365H,
  B365D,
  B365A,
  ( (CASE WHEN B365H IS NOT NULL THEN B365H ELSE NULL END) +
    (CASE WHEN BWH IS NOT NULL THEN BWH ELSE 0 END) +
    (CASE WHEN IWH IS NOT NULL THEN IWH ELSE 0 END)
  ) / ( (CASE WHEN B365H IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN BWH IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN IWH IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ) AS mean_home_odds
FROM Match

params.description: Per-match row of selected betting odds and a computed mean of available home-win odds — answers questions about match-level bookmaker odds and a simple averaged home-win price.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve bookmaker odds (Bet365 home/draw/away) for a specific match (by id or match_api_id). | Compare home-side odds across matches or teams. | Compose further match-level metrics that use per-match odds (e.g., merge with match outcomes to compute implied probabilities). | Join odds to one-row-per-match dimensions (team, competition, season) without needing additional aggregation.
params.output_schema: id: primary key of the Match row (Match.id) — one row per match in this view. | match_api_id: external match identifier from Match.match_api_id. | home_team_api_id: home team external identifier from Match.home_team_api_id. | away_team_api_id: away team external identifier from Match.away_team_api_id. | B365H: Bet365 decimal odds for a home win, from Match.B365H (NULL if not recorded). | B365D: Bet365 decimal odds for a draw, from Match.B365D (NULL if not recorded). | B365A: Bet365 decimal odds for an away win, from Match.B365A (NULL if not recorded). | mean_home_odds: mean of available home-win odds across three bookmakers (B365H, BWH, IWH) computed per the expression below; NULL when B365H is NULL and no other contributing terms are present per the expression's denominator logic.
params.grounded_columns: Match.id | Match.match_api_id | Match.home_team_api_id | Match.away_team_api_id | Match.B365H | Match.B365D | Match.B365A | Match.BWH | Match.IWH
params.metric: mean_home_odds = ( (CASE WHEN Match.B365H IS NOT NULL THEN Match.B365H ELSE NULL END) + (CASE WHEN Match.BWH IS NOT NULL THEN Match.BWH ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN Match.IWH IS NOT NULL THEN Match.IWH ELSE 0 END) ) / ( (CASE WHEN Match.B365H IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN Match.BWH IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN Match.IWH IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ) | Note: expression treats B365H specially by placing NULL (which behaves like adding NULL) when B365H IS NULL — functionally this causes the numerator to be NULL if B365H is NULL while still counting BWH and IWH in numerator as 0 when absent. The denominator counts only non-NULL contributors among B365H, BWH, IWH.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to one-row-per-match or one-row-per-team dimensions on the listed keys — these joins will not duplicate measures. | Safe: join to match_basic_outcomes on Match.id = match_basic_outcomes.id — safe because both are one-row-per-match (AGG/NORM views aligned to the match id), so mean_home_odds will not be duplicated. | Safe: join to team_latest_attributes on home_team_api_id = team_latest_attributes.team_api_id (or away_team_api_id = team_latest_attributes.team_api_id) — safe when team_latest_attributes is one-row-per-team (RANK) so joining on team_api_id does not multiply match rows. | Safe: join to player_identity only when joining on a one-to-one key (e.g., if you only attach a single player-level identifier per match via a pre-aggregated key). | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables or views without re-aggregation: examples include match_lineup_players_unpivot (RESHAPE) which has many players per match. Joining this view directly to match_lineup_players_unpivot on id will multiply match rows by number of lineup players and thus will duplicate mean_home_odds and other per-match measures. Instead, either: | - aggregate the one-to-many side to one row per match (e.g., count players per match) before joining, or | - join and then re-aggregate results back to match grain, using SUM/AVG on measures that are intended to be combined, and ensuring measures from this view are not double-counted. | Do NOT join to sibling views that are at a finer grain (e.g., player_latest_attributes) without first reducing that sibling to match-level keys. Any join that maps one row in this view to multiple rows in the other side will multiply per-match measures. | When composing additional metrics: treat this view's outputs as match-grain base measures. If your downstream query needs per-team-season aggregations, aggregate mean_home_odds appropriately (e.g., AVG(mean_home_odds) grouped by team and season) after joining only to safe dimensions or after pre-aggregating one-to-many details.

Provides B365 and a simple mean_odds across available bookmakers (ignores NULLs). Useful for studies comparing implied probabilities vs outcomes. | Use for: Compare odds to match outcomes; Filter matches by odds ranges; Use mean odds as feature in prediction

SELECT
  league_id,
  season,
  COALESCE(SUM(COALESCE(home_team_goal,0) + COALESCE(away_team_goal,0)), 0) AS total_goals,
  COUNT(id) AS match_count
FROM Match
GROUP BY league_id, season

Derived from SUM(COALESCE(Match.home_team_goal,0) + COALESCE(Match.away_team_goal,0)). If no rows exist, COALESCE ensures 0. | match_count: number of Match rows (matches) in that league-season. Derived from COUNT(Match.id).
params.grounded_columns: Match.league_id | Match.season | Match.home_team_goal | Match.away_team_goal | Match.id
params.metric: total_goals = COALESCE(SUM(COALESCE(Match.home_team_goal, 0) + COALESCE(Match.away_team_goal, 0)), 0) | match_count = COUNT(Match.id)

Instead, either: (a) join and then re-aggregate after the join at the desired grain, or (b) join from Match to this view only on exact (league_id, season) keys and use the view's measures solely as contextual attributes (being careful not to SUM them again). | do NOT join to one-to-many sibling views such as match_lineup_players_unpivot or player_latest_attributes without re-aggregating, because those views expand match-related rows (players, lineups) and would multiply league-season measures unless you first collapse the many-side to one row per (league_id, season) or re-aggregate after the join. | safe composition pattern for derived metrics: to compute goals_per_match at league-season grain, compute goals_per_match = total_goals / NULLIF(match_count, 0) directly from this view (no additional joins required). | when composing into a larger query at a coarser grain (e.g., league across multiple seasons), aggregate this view's measures (SUM(total_goals), SUM(match_count)) — this preserves correctness because the view is already at one row per league-season and aggregation over those rows does not cause duplication.

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_identity on player_identity.player_api_id = player_attributes_events.player_api_id — safe because player_identity is a one-row-per-player identity dimension so it will not duplicate attribute snapshot rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_latest_attributes on player_latest_attributes.player_api_id = player_attributes_events.player_api_id AND player_latest_attributes.date = player_attributes_events.date — safe when constrained to matching date and id because both sides represent specific snapshots; ensure the join keys include the snapshot id/date to avoid duplication. | do NOT join to match_lineup_players_unpivot (RESHAPE) or match_rows (SEL) or match_basic_outcomes (NORM) without aggregating first — those views can contain many match rows per player or per match and would produce one-to-many duplication of attribute snapshot rows and thereby inflate any aggregates computed directly on sprint_speed/overall_rating/potential. | do NOT join directly to match_goals_by_league_season or match_team_odds (AGG) without aligning keys and re-aggregating: these are aggregated measures at match/season/team grain and could duplicate attribute snapshot rows if joined on non-unique keys. | If you need player-level aggregates (e.g., average sprint_speed per player), perform GROUP BY player_api_id (or player_identity key) on player_attributes_events before joining to any one-to-many fact tables — this preserves correct cardinality and avoids double-counting. | When joining to teams_dim or team_attributes_rows, ensure the join key is a unique team identifier and that you join on a matching snapshot date or aggregate player attributes to team-level first; otherwise team-level joins that are one-to-many will multiply player snapshot rows.

views.name: player_max_attribute_by_period
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pae.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  MAX(pae.sprint_speed) AS max_sprint_speed,
  MAX(pae.overall_rating) AS max_overall_rating,
  MAX(pae.potential) AS max_potential,
  COUNT(*) AS records_in_period
FROM player_attributes_events pae
GROUP BY pae.player_api_id

params.description: For each player (player_api_id), returns the maximum observed attribute values (sprint_speed, overall_rating, potential) and the count of attribute records in the source period.
params.when_to_use: Report maximum player attribute values over the entire source period (e.g., best observed sprint speed, highest overall rating, highest potential per player). | As a building block when you need one-row-per-player summary metrics to join to player dimension or match-level rows without duplicating measures. | When comparing players by their historical maxima or filtering players by their peak attributes (e.g., players with max_overall_rating >= X). | As input to further aggregation (team- or league-level maxima/averages) where the planner must treat these as already-aggregated per-player measures.
params.output_schema: player_api_id: unique identifier for the player (derived from player_attributes_events.player_api_id) | max_sprint_speed: maximum sprint_speed observed for this player in player_attributes_events (derived from MAX(player_attributes_events.sprint_speed)) | max_overall_rating: maximum overall_rating observed for this player in player_attributes_events (derived from MAX(player_attributes_events.overall_rating)) | max_potential: maximum potential observed for this player in player_attributes_events (derived from MAX(player_attributes_events.potential)) | records_in_period: count of player_attributes_events rows for this player in the source period (derived from COUNT(*) on player_attributes_events grouped by player_api_id)
params.grounded_columns: player_attributes_events.player_api_id | player_attributes_events.sprint_speed | player_attributes_events.overall_rating | player_attributes_events.potential
params.metric: max_sprint_speed = MAX(player_attributes_events.sprint_speed)  -- per player_api_id | max_overall_rating = MAX(player_attributes_events.overall_rating)  -- per player_api_id | max_potential = MAX(player_attributes_events.potential)  -- per player_api_id | records_in_period = COUNT(*)  -- number of player_attributes_events rows aggregated per player_api_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_identity on player_api_id — safe because this view has exactly one row per player_api_id (one-row-per-key), so joining to the player dimension (one row per player_api_id) will not duplicate these measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to matches_core or match_rows only if you aggregate or otherwise handle the one-to-many relationship from matches to players. Joining this view directly to match-level tables (one match row to many players) will multiply the player's aggregated measures across match rows unless you re-aggregate after the join. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_latest_attributes or teams_dim on team id only after ensuring a one-to-one relationship (e.g., via team id in player_identity). If you join this view to a team-level table that has multiple rows per team without re-aggregating, team-level measures will be duplicated. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many event/detail tables (for example match_lineup_players_unpivot, match_goals_by_league_season, match_team_odds) without re-aggregation or using distinct keys: those tables can have multiple rows per player_api_id (per match or event), and joining them directly will multiply the per-player aggregates in this view. | recommended composition patterns: | - To produce team-level maxima or averages of player maxima: join this view to player_identity to get the player's team_id at the desired time (or to player_latest_attributes if you need current team), then GROUP BY team_id and apply aggregation (e.g., MAX(max_overall_rating) or AVG(max_sprint_speed)). This re-aggregates the one-row-per-player measures safely. | - To filter players by peak attributes and then join to match data: first filter this view (e.g., WHERE max_overall_rating >= X) to get a set of player_api_id, then join that set to match_lineup_players_unpivot or matches_core; still be aware that joining to match-level rows will produce multiple rows per player (one per match) — if you want per-player measures remain unchanged, keep them in the SELECT as-is or re-aggregate after the join as appropriate. | - To enrich with identity attributes: join player_max_attribute_by_period.player_api_id = player_identity.player_api_id (one-to-one) — safe because both sides are one row per player_api_id.

params.description: Provides one-row-per-match identifiers and basic match keys (id, league_id, match_api_id) for composing match-level analyses.
params.when_to_use: Look up canonical match identifiers for joining match-level metrics or dimensions | Build or filter match-level aggregates (goals, odds, lineups) by match id or league | Seed queries that require one row per match before joining additional match-related facts
params.output_schema: id: unique match identifier (derived from Match.id) | league_id: identifier of the league this match belongs to (derived from Match.league_id) | match_api_id: external API identifier for the match (derived from Match.match_api_id)
params.grounded_columns: Match.id | Match.league_id | Match.match_api_id
params.metric: id = Match.id | league_id = Match.league_id | match_api_id = Match.match_api_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to league_basic(NORM) on league_basic.id = match_row_level_cohort.league_id — safe because league_basic is one-row-per-league so it will not duplicate match rows or measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to matches_core(SEL) on matches_core.id = match_row_level_cohort.id — safe if matches_core is one-row-per-match (acts as a same-grain enrichment), it will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_basic_outcomes(NORM) on match_basic_outcomes.id = match_row_level_cohort.id — safe when match_basic_outcomes is one-row-per-match; use this to add match-level outcome metrics without re-aggregation. | DO NOT join directly to match_lineup_players_unpivot(RESHAPE) on id without aggregation first, because match_lineup_players_unpivot is many-rows-per-match (one row per lineup player) and would multiply match-level rows/measures. Instead aggregate lineup rows to match-level (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT player_id) per match) before joining. | DO NOT join directly to match_goals_by_league_season(AGG) or match_team_odds(AGG) without checking their grain; if they are aggregated at match-level (one row per match), join on id is safe. If they are aggregated at a different grain (e.g., team-by-match or league-season), re-aggregate or join on matching keys to avoid duplication. | DO NOT join directly to team_attributes_rows(SEL), team_latest_attributes(RANK), player_latest_attributes(RANK), or match_rows(SEL) if those views are many-to-one or one-to-many relative to match: ensure you join on a matching one-row-per-match key or aggregate the many-side first. | General rule: this view is strictly one-row-per Match.id (grain = ['id']). Any join partner that is also one-row-per-match (or one-row-per-league when joining by league_id) is safe and will not duplicate measures. For one-to-many partners, either aggregate them to match-level before joining or join and then re-aggregate to restore match grain.

params.description: Counts of matches per league (one row per league): how many Match rows are associated with each League.id.
params.when_to_use: Get the total number of matches in each league (reporting or dashboarding). | Join match counts onto league-level records to show match volumes per league. | Compose league-level rate/ratio metrics where the denominator is number of matches per league. | Filter or rank leagues by match volume before further league-level analysis.
params.output_schema: league_id: the League.id value identifying the league (derived from League.id) | match_count: the number of Match rows associated with that League.id (derived from COUNT(Match.id))
params.grounded_columns: League.id | Match.id | Match.league_id
params.metric: match_count = COUNT(Match.id)  -- aggregate count of Match rows per League.id as computed by the SQL GROUP BY
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to league_basic (or any one-row-per-league view/table) on league_id = id — safe because this view is one-row-per League.id, so joining will not duplicate match_count. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to teams_dim on league_id = teams_dim.league_id ONLY IF teams_dim is guaranteed one-row-per-league (verify teams_dim grain). If teams_dim is many-teams-per-league, this will duplicate match_count and is NOT safe without re-aggregation. | do NOT join directly to any one-to-many detail tables or views (for example Match, match_rows, match_goals_by_league_season, match_lineup_players_unpivot, match_team_odds, matches_core, match_basic_outcomes, player_latest_attributes, team_latest_attributes, player_identity, team_attributes_rows) without re-aggregating the detail to league level first — joining them as-is will multiply rows and thus inflate match_count. | If you need to combine match_count with another one-to-many measure (for example total goals by league season), first aggregate that measure to the same league grain (one row per League.id) and then join on league_id. Example safe pattern: derive goals_by_league = SUM(goals) GROUP BY league_id, then join goals_by_league to this view on league_id. | When composing into higher-level metrics (rates, averages per match), treat match_count as a pre-aggregated denominator at league grain; do not sum match_count across leagues and expect detail-level semantics unless that is the intended aggregation.

params.when_to_use: Look up the latest overall_rating, potential, preferred_foot, height, and weight for a specific player_api_id. | Join latest player attribute snapshot as a dimension to match- or event-level data when you need each player's most recent attributes. | Compute aggregates across players (e.g., average overall_rating by preferred_foot) using the latest attributes. | Compose into player-level modeling features where exactly one row per player is required.

params.metric: overall_rating = pal.overall_rating  -- direct attribute from player_attributes_latest (no aggregation in this view) | potential = pal.potential  -- direct attribute from player_attributes_latest | preferred_foot = pal.preferred_foot  -- direct attribute from player_attributes_latest | height = p.height  -- direct attribute from Player table | weight = p.weight  -- direct attribute from Player table
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_identity on player_api_id — safe because both this view and player_identity are one-row-per-player (player_api_id) so measures from this snapshot will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to teams_dim or league_basic when linking by team_id or league_id after ensuring you have a single team/league key per row — safe when the join key is one-to-one from this view's row to the target dimension. | do NOT join directly to match-level or event-level tables (for example match_rows, matches_core, match_basic_outcomes, match_goals_by_league_season, match_lineup_players_unpivot) without aggregation or additional join constraints — those are one-to-many relative to player_api_id (a player appears in many matches/events) and would duplicate this view's per-player measures. | do NOT join directly to team_attributes_rows or other time-series/rows tables that are one-to-many per player_api_id or per team without re-aggregating to the same grain (player_api_id) or applying a row-selection (e.g., latest per player) — otherwise measures like overall_rating will be multiplied. | If you need player attributes repeated per match (match-level analysis), first choose the join semantics and cardinality explicitly: either (a) join this view to matches on player_api_id AND match date with an appropriate date filter (e.g., attributes.date <= match.date) while selecting one attribute row per match (e.g., nearest prior snapshot), or (b) aggregate match-level rows after the join to avoid duplicating player measures. | When composing metrics: treat all listed metrics as point-in-time attributes (not aggregates). If you join to other one-to-many tables and then aggregate, aggregate original attribute columns as required (e.g., AVG(overall_rating) or MAX(overall_rating)) rather than assuming they remain single-valued.

views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  p.player_name AS player_name,
  -- normalize height: keep NULLs as allowed; otherwise cast to numeric
  CASE
    WHEN p.height IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE p.height
  END AS height,
  CASE
    WHEN p.weight IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE p.weight
  END AS weight,
  p.birthday AS birthday,
  p.player_fifa_api_id AS player_fifa_api_id
FROM Player p
WHERE p.player_api_id IS NOT NULL

params.description: Provides one-row-per-player core identifying attributes (name, height, weight, birthday, FIFA id) for players present in the Player table.
params.when_to_use: Look up basic player attributes (name, height, weight, birthday, FIFA id) by player_api_id. | Join player identifying attributes into match- or team-level datasets when you need stable, non-aggregated player fields. | Seed for further compositions that compute player-level metrics (e.g., age, BMI) or to enrich event/lineup rows with player metadata.
params.output_schema: player_api_id: unique player identifier at the granularity of this view (derived from Player.player_api_id). | player_name: player's full name (derived from Player.player_name). | height: player's height value as stored in Player.height; NULLs preserved (derived from Player.height). | weight: player's weight value as stored in Player.weight; NULLs preserved (derived from Player.weight). | birthday: player's date of birth (derived from Player.birthday). | player_fifa_api_id: alternative FIFA id for the player (derived from Player.player_fifa_api_id).
params.grounded_columns: Player.player_api_id | Player.player_name | Player.height | Player.weight | Player.birthday | Player.player_fifa_api_id
params.metric: player_api_id = identity(Player.player_api_id) | player_name = identity(Player.player_name) | height = identity(Player.height) -- NULL preserved; no numeric cast applied beyond pass-through | weight = identity(Player.weight) -- NULL preserved; no numeric cast applied beyond pass-through | birthday = identity(Player.birthday) | player_fifa_api_id = identity(Player.player_fifa_api_id)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensions that are one-row-per-player on player_api_id — e.g., join to player_identity on player_api_id — safe because player_basic_attributes is one-row-per-player_api_id and those dimension views are expected to be one-row-per-player (joins will not duplicate measures). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match-level or lineup-level rows by player_api_id only when those rows are the many side; e.g., joining this view (one row per player) into match_lineup_players_unpivot (many rows per match/player occurrence) is safe because the planner is enriching many-side rows with player attributes per occurrence (measures from player_basic_attributes are not aggregated but simply attached row-wise). | do NOT join this view to one-to-many tables/views on player_api_id when the intent is to preserve the one-row-per-player aggregation of measures without re-aggregation — for example, joining to a goals/events table aggregated at event-level or to team_attributes_rows (if it contains multiple rows per player) will duplicate player rows and multiply any derived player-level measures unless you first aggregate the many-side to one row per player (e.g., SUM/COUNT by player_api_id) or otherwise deduplicate. | do NOT join to sibling AGG/RANK/RESHAPE views that are many-per-player (for example, match_goals_by_league_season or team_attributes_rows if they are many-per-player) without explicit grouping/aggregation on the many-side, because that will produce multiple rows per player and duplicate the player_basic_attributes row across them. | recommended pattern: when building player-level metrics, start from this view (one row per player_api_id) and LEFT JOIN aggregates computed from event/goal/match tables that have been pre-aggregated to player_api_id to avoid accidental row multiplication.

params.when_to_use: Retrieve a player's attribute snapshot (overall_rating, potential, preferred_foot, height, weight) for a specific Player_Attributes.id or player_api_id at the exact recorded date. | Compose time-series analyses by treating each Player_Attributes.id / Player_Attributes.date as a snapshot grain for a player. | Join player identity info (name, fifa id) to attribute snapshots for reporting or downstream aggregations (e.g., average overall_rating by season after proper aggregation). | Build metrics that aggregate player attribute values (e.g., average overall_rating per player, max potential per player) by aggregating this view, not by joining other one-to-many tables into it directly.
params.output_schema: player_api_id: player_api_id from Player table (p.player_api_id). The player's internal API identifier used as a join key. | player_name: player_name from Player table (p.player_name). The player's name as recorded in Player. | player_fifa_api_id: player_fifa_api_id from Player table (p.player_fifa_api_id). FIFA identifier from Player. | Player_Attributes.id: id from Player_Attributes table (pa.id). Primary key of the attribute snapshot row — this view's snapshot-level unique identifier. | Player_Attributes.date: date from Player_Attributes table (pa.date). Date when the attributes were recorded (snapshot date). | overall_rating: overall_rating from Player_Attributes table (pa.overall_rating). Player's overall rating at this snapshot (nullable numeric). | potential: potential from Player_Attributes table (pa.potential). Player's potential rating at this snapshot (nullable numeric). | preferred_foot: preferred_foot from Player_Attributes table (pa.preferred_foot). Player's preferred foot text at this snapshot. | height: height from Player table (p.height). Player height (copied from Player at join time). | weight: weight from Player table (p.weight). Player weight (copied from Player at join time).
params.grounded_columns: Player_Attributes.id | Player_Attributes.date | Player_Attributes.player_api_id | Player_Attributes.overall_rating | Player_Attributes.potential | Player_Attributes.preferred_foot | Player.player_api_id | Player.player_name | Player.player_fifa_api_id | Player.height | Player.weight
params.metric: overall_rating = direct passthrough of pa.overall_rating (no aggregation). Treat as a measure only after you apply an aggregate (e.g., AVG(overall_rating) BY player_api_id). | potential = direct passthrough of pa.potential (no aggregation). Treat as a measure only after you apply an aggregate. | snapshot_count = COUNT(Player_Attributes.id) when counting snapshots; define only via aggregation on Player_Attributes.id (this view is at snapshot grain so COUNT(*) or COUNT(Player_Attributes.id) yields number of snapshots).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_identity on player_api_id (player_identity.player_api_id) — safe because this view is already joined to Player and is one row per Player_Attributes.id; joining to a one-row-per-player identity view will not duplicate snapshot-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to teams_dim or league_basic on appropriate keys only when those dims are one-row-per-key and you are joining at the same grain (e.g., if you aggregate snapshots to player level first). Directly joining teams_dim (team-level) is safe only if you aggregate snapshots to player-level or join on a player->team key that is one-to-one for the snapshot rows. | do NOT join this view directly to a one-to-many fact (e.g., match_rows, match_goals_by_league_season, match_lineup_players_unpivot) without first aggregating or deduplicating, because those will multiply snapshot rows: for example, joining match_lineup_players_unpivot (many matches per player) to this snapshot view will duplicate a snapshot for each match the player appears in, inflating measures like overall_rating unless you aggregate (e.g., AVG(overall_rating) with appropriate GROUP BY) or first reduce the many-side to one row per player per time window. | do NOT join this view to Player_Attributes again or any table that contains multiple attribute snapshots per Player_Attributes.id because Player_Attributes.id is the unique snapshot key in this view; joining on player_api_id to another snapshot-level table without aligning on date/id will produce a many-to-many expansion. | recommended composition pattern: if you need player-level measures (one row per player), aggregate this view: SELECT player_api_id, MAX(player_name) ..., AVG(overall_rating) AS avg_overall_rating FROM player_attribute_snapshots GROUP BY player_api_id. After aggregation to player-level, it is safe to join to team or match-level tables on player_api_id provided those joins are one-to-one from the planner's perspective or the other side is aggregated down to one row per player. | when joining to sibling views that are RANK or AGG (e.g., player_latest_attributes which is already one-row-per-player), prefer joining on player_api_id to avoid duplication because player_latest_attributes is one-row-per-player and this view is one-row-per-snapshot; join only after aggregating or filtering this view to one-row-per-player (for example, filter by Player_Attributes.id = latest id) to ensure row multiplicity remains controlled.

  player_api_id,
  COUNT(overall_rating) AS rating_count,
  AVG(overall_rating) AS avg_overall_rating,
  MIN(overall_rating) AS min_overall_rating,
  MAX(overall_rating) AS max_overall_rating,
  -- latest overall_rating by most recent date per player
  (SELECT pa2.overall_rating
   FROM Player_Attributes pa2
   WHERE pa2.player_api_id = pa.player_api_id
     AND pa2.overall_rating IS NOT NULL
   ORDER BY datetime(pa2.date) DESC
   LIMIT 1) AS latest_overall_rating,
  (SELECT pa3.date
   FROM Player_Attributes pa3
   WHERE pa3.player_api_id = pa.player_api_id
     AND pa3.overall_rating IS NOT NULL
   ORDER BY datetime(pa3.date) DESC
   LIMIT 1) AS latest_rating_date
FROM Player_Attributes pa
WHERE pa.overall_rating IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY player_api_id
